We were never on any lines. There were no lines at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were interrogated in the restaurant by these two soldiers who were always the same, the questions that they asked you, what was the objective of these questions? What did they want to find out from you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: The objective was to find out about arms, the whereabouts of the Croatian units, their strengths. They wanted to know things that we didn't know anything about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was that an oral interrogation or did you have to put your questions in writing? Did they write anything down during these interrogations?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: This was more like a provocation, without any notes being taken. People were just ill-treated, physically abused, kicked and hit. One young man, whose name is Ivica Jankovic, he was seriously injured in the head. They didn't want to administer first aid. We, other detainees, tried to help him, to stop his bleeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While you were in the blacksmith's shop, did the Red Cross visit you? Did anybody else visit you? Did the members of your family visit you? Did anybody visit you during the stay in the blacksmith's shop?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: From the time we were arrested, when the conflict started, a few days later the Red Cross representatives tried to enter Mehurici; however, the Mujahedins and the MOS wouldn't allow them to do that. And it was only at their ninth or tenth attempt that they managed to reach us and register us. If they hadn't done that, I'm sure that I would not be alive today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they came to the blacksmith's shop to see you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: Yes. They came to see us. They registered us. And we were given Red Cross cards with our names on them and other details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: You have just told us that you are a 70-per cent invalid. Who is it who accorded you the disability? Is there a commission who accorded you this disability status?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have documents. And as for my disability status, it was accorded to me after the exchange in Zepce. When I joined the HVO, two or three months later I was heavily wounded. I was treated. And in respect of my detention and the injury that I sustained later on, I was accorded 70-per cent-disability status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I'm going to give the floor to the Defence for their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Tadic. I'm Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for General Hadzihasanovic. I'm going to ask you just a few questions to clarify some things. You have stated that after the 8th of June a number of other people were brought to the blacksmith's shop. One of them was wounded. Is it true that this was Zeljko Puselja?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm 1.000 per cent certain. He had escaped an execution site. He was recaptured and brought to the blacksmith's shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When he entered, you immediately saw that his arm was dressed.

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had his arm fractured. He was heavily wounded. And the lad is today --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Zeljko Puselja told you that another HVO soldier had also managed to escape the execution site? His name is Darko Puselja. He was also heavily wounded and he was immediately transferred to the hospital in Zenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: Darko Puselja was not an HVO soldier. He was a minor at the time. It is true that at the moment when the execution was being carried out in Bikose, he was there. He managed to escape the execution site. He was captured and transferred to the hospital in Zenica. And then through some channels from that hospital, he managed to join his relatives in Zenica. So he was not executed at the end of the day. That's what I'm trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've also told us that after the exchange of civilians, you worked on the cleaning detail around the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were on the cleaning detail around the school, you never entered the school; you never climbed to go to the first, second, or the third floor.

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: We only went to the first floor. And on that day, we were all beaten by the soldiers who were hanging around the corridors. They held wooden batons in their hands. They asked us to take some garbage. We were cleaning some sewage pipes around the school, and then on the windows we could see people and we could hear shouts coming through the windows from the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were on the cleaning detail and while you were being taken for interrogation, you were guarded by the civilian police from Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: VINKO TADIC
utterances.text: We were not guarded by the civilian police. We were guarded by some other people whom I knew by sight. I knew even some of their names. I can't remember their names at the moment. In any case, I knew them by sight. I still know them. They were not civilian policemen. They were reserve police or some service. I don't know what kind of service they were. They didn't wear civilian police uniforms, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm turning to the other Defence counsel. Mr. Dixon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Dixon. I'm turning towards the Prosecution. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, there'll be no re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Witness, your testimony is hereby finished. You have answered the questions put to you both by the Prosecution and the Defence. We would like to thank you for your contribution towards finding the truth. We wish you a happy journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask Madam Usher to take you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have completed the week. Next week -- is the Prosecution able to give us their plan for next week? I'm giving the floor to Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, next week the Prosecution will present five witnesses. Yesterday in the afternoon the updated and amended witness schedule list for next week has been filed. There's basically only a change in order of the witnesses and one replacement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We have a witness -- one witness on Monday; two on Tuesday; one on Wednesday; one on Thursday; and two witnesses on Friday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Next week we shall sit on -- in the afternoon on Monday to Thursday and on Friday we shall sit in the morning. I understand the Defence wanted to know whether there will be an interruption during which they will be able to regulate the issue of the archives of the European Union. As I have already indicated to you, there will be a day off on the 2nd February, which is a bank holiday, and we are also going to have the 6th of February on Friday off because the courtroom has to undergo regular maintenance. So the first week of February, two days will be off. The first one will be a bank holiday, and the second one will be Friday, which is scheduled for maintenance. So you will have two days during which you will be able to gain access to the archives to the extent to which you will have the possibility to access the documentation. I also understand that you wanted to find out about the Easter period during April. It seems to me at the moment that Friday will be a bank holiday and Monday will be a bank holiday. In April there, will be two days without sitting: The Good Friday and the Easter Monday. I don't know the dates. If the Defence counsel believe that they need more days in order to be able to prepare, you can tell us, but please do it as soon as possible. Let us know so I can advice the Registry. We will then be able to plan for the months of March and April. If you estimate that during the Easter period you will need a few more days for preparation, bear in mind that we already have two days of bank holiday. That's Easter -- that's Good Friday and Easter Monday. Do the parties have any remarks at this point? I'm turning towards the Defence. Any questions? Any issues to be raised? I'm turning towards the Prosecution. Any issues to be raised at this stage? Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honours, since we have now been informed that Friday, the 6th of February there will be no court session, I wish to use this opportunity to emphasise and to request that this day doesn't count against the half-year's time frame the Prosecution has been given to present its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the 6th of February, it appears on the provisional schedule of the Registry, which indicated that there was court maintenance on the 6th of February. Having exhausted the agenda for this sitting, we will adjourn, and we will all meet again on Monday at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of January, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.58 a.m.,
